newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks reverse course to end slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks reverse course to end slightly up.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks shrugged off comments made by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan to end higher on Thursday, buoyed by interest in China-related issues and selective buying amid the blue chips.

The Hang Seng Index rose 4.77 points, or 0.04 percent, to close at 13,546.60 after spending most of the day in negative territory due to Greenspan's hints to the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday that U.S. interest rates may rise.

"People see Greenspan's comments as more smoke than fire. He has said this before and only had a really short-term effect on market," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. Greenspan said in his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony that the Fed may raise rates before inflation picks up.
"It is conceivable...to have to move before you see actual evidences of real inflation emerging," Greenspan said.
The comments sent Dow industrials down 55.03 points to 6,983.18 on Wednesday. The U.S. long bond tumbled 1-16/32 to yield 6.77 percent.

But brokers said the Hong Kong market had not been following the U.S. markets closely of late. "We are looking north for indications. As long as the economy in China prospers, stocks will move more in tandem with China," said Mak.
China-related issues continued to perform strongly on Thursday, with the H-share index of mainland Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong rising 29.90 points, or 2.98 percent, to 1,032.49.
Property stocks were mixed ahead of the launch in March of residential property sales at some major developers.
Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$0.25 to HK$90.50 but Henderson Land closed unchanged at HK$70.50 and Hang Lung Development fell HK$0.20 to HK$15.70.
Amoy Properties finished down HK$0.15 at HK$9.50.
"After the recent correction, property stocks should be a good buy now. We are positive on the long-term property outlook," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
He expected upcoming property sales to meet with strong demand.
Thursday's turnover was a healthy HK$10.85 billion compared with HK$10.25 billion on Wednesday.
February Hang Seng Index futures expired on Thursday and closed on a loss of 57 points at 13,498.
